items.summary: Program that held down premiums won’t be renewed for 2027, resulting in higher costs for some seniors.

items.title: Why Prices Could Rise for Medicare Drug Plans Next Year
items.summary: Medicare beneficiaries may face higher premiums next year for their Part D drug plans, as the federal government plans to end subsidies that helped mitigate price increases in the program.  The Trump administration will not continue the subsidies beyond 2026, The Wall Street Journal reported.  About 25 million Medicare recipients are enrolled in a stand-alone Part D plan for their drug coverage.
